text:
maya: Heads-up — my docs PR is failing the docs-preview CI and I think it's because of an SDK snippet that assumes the old API default.

maya: CI error: `docs-preview: snippet-runner exited with code 1` and the log points to the `client.generate()` example.

sam: can you paste the snippet?

maya: sure — here's the block I added in the migration guide:

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood();

// old example relied on default model routing
const out = await client.generate({
  prompt: 'Summarize the meeting',
});
console.log(out.text);
```

maya: docs-preview complains about missing `model` field now. locally, runtime routes to a default but the snippet runner uses strict validation.

devin: right — we tightened the snippet-runner to require explicit `model` or `route` for reproducibility. We shipped that change in runtime v0.9.0. docs PRs that rely on implicit defaults will fail.

harper: is the fix adding `model: 'redwood-rlhf-1'` to the snippet? or should we change the snippet-runner to accept the old behavior?

devin: prefer changing the snippet — explicit is better for docs. Also avoids accidental runtime differences between hosted/dedicated/private.

sam: +1. Which model should we recommend in the migration guide? The guide aims at customers moving from hosted -> dedicated.

devin: use `model: 'rwd-base-bert-1'` for a deterministic example (small, cheap) and add a note: "pick a model matching your deployment mode".

maya: ok I'll update. quick Q: how strict should the snippet be about other config defaults? like `temperature` and `max_tokens`?

devin: set `temperature: 0.2` and `max_tokens: 150` explicitly in examples that demonstrate summaries. Mention in a parenthetical that defaults differ by runtime.

maya: got it. Also found one dead link in the migration guide to `docs/examples/sdk-quickstart` — docs-bot flagged 404.

docs-bot: :robot_face: Broken link detected in `docs/migrations/hosted-to-dedicated.md` -> `/docs/examples/sdk-quickstart` (404).

harper: thanks — was going to fix that in a follow-up. If you update the snippet and the link, can we merge once CI passes? Any reviewer needs to re-run the preview?

sam: assign me as reviewer. if CI passes I can approve and we can merge. we should wait for the preview job though — it verifies the snippet output.

maya: assigning sam now. Updating snippet + link in the same PR. 

maya: pushing new commit. snippet now: 

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });

const out = await client.generate({
  model: 'rwd-base-bert-1',
  prompt: 'Summarize the meeting',
  temperature: 0.2,
  max_tokens: 150
});
console.log(out.text);
```

maya: CI queued the docs-preview again (job 4729).

docs-bot: :white_check_mark: docs-preview succeeded for commit f3b2c9 (job 4729) — snippet runner output matched expected snapshot.

sam: reviewing now. looks good to me, nothing surprising. Approving.

sam: small nit — add a short note in the migration guide that "if you rely on runtime routing in production, include `route` config for private deployments".

maya: added that line. CI re-ran quick lint and preview succeeded.

sam: LGTM — merging after lunch to avoid late-night deploys.

harper: sweet. thanks for moving quickly. I'll follow up with a separate PR to add a short section about snippet-runner validation to the docs contributor guide so future PRs are less likely to break. :sparkles:
